name: Aryan Singh
summary: I build low-latency trading systems, and fix bugs in the AI and data tools teams run in production.
about: I like building things that solve real problems. Watching an idea turn into something that actually runs is what gives me the kick, and it's what keeps me going when a bug has been winning for hours.

Most of my work sits where finance meets systems engineering. I build order books and matching engines, and chase the questions that matter in high-frequency trading: how fast it is, how predictable it is, and whether every state change can be replayed and checked.

I also fix bugs upstream in open-source AI and data tooling, from agent frameworks to data pipelines, because reading other people's production code is the fastest way I know to get better at writing my own.
Three of my projects have published patents: Smart Flow Analysis and Trade Execution, Readease, and Dropr.

featured.title: Order book and matching engine
featured.blurb: Multi-instrument C++20 limit order book with price-time priority, deterministic event replay, queue-position tracking and latency benchmarks.

featured.title: Smart flow analysis
featured.blurb: Tracks institutional mutual fund flows, ranks stocks by alpha, and executes approved trades through Zerodha.

featured.title: Readease
featured.blurb: Helps students with dyslexia read class material: OCR, AI simplification, text-to-speech and translation.

featured.title: Dropr
featured.blurb: Campus peer-to-peer delivery: students post errands, others pick them up, with live chat and order tracking.

featured.title: Fund data pipeline
featured.blurb: Parses 134 mutual fund disclosure files into Delta tables for fund-level and cross-fund Pareto analysis.
